nodes.label: Go (Golang) Security Spec (Go 1.25.x, Standard Library, net/http)
GO-DEPLOY-001: Keep the Go toolchain and standard library updated (security releases)
requirements: - MUST run a supported Go major release and apply patch releases promptly.
- SHOULD treat patch releases as security-relevant, even if your application code didn’t change.
fixes: - Upgrade to the latest patch of a supported Go version.
- Add an automated check (CI) that fails when Go is below an approved minimum.
nodes.rationale: Keep the Go toolchain and standard library updated (security releases)

nodes.label: GO-SUPPLY-001: Go module authenticity MUST NOT be disabled for public dependencies
requirements: - MUST keep module checksum verification enabled for public modules.
- SHOULD commit `go.sum` and treat changes as security-sensitive.
- MUST NOT use insecure module fetching settings for public modules.
- MAY configure private module behavior using `GOPRIVATE`/`GONOSUMDB` for private repos, but must do so narrowly and intentionally.
fixes: - Restore defaults for public module verification.
- For private modules:
- Set `GOPRIVATE=your.private.domain/*`
- Configure an internal proxy or direct fetching, and restrict `GONOSUMDB` to private patterns only.
nodes.rationale: Go module authenticity MUST NOT be disabled for public dependencies

nodes.label: GO-CONFIG-001: Secrets must be externalized and never logged or committed
requirements: - MUST load secrets from environment variables, secret managers, or secure config files with restricted permissions.
- MUST NOT hard-code secrets in Go source, test fixtures that may reach production, or build args.
- MUST NOT log secrets or full credential-bearing connection strings.
- SHOULD fail closed in production if required secrets are missing.
fixes: - Move secrets to a secret store / environment variables.
- Redact sensitive fields in logs.
- Add secret scanning to CI and pre-commit.
nodes.rationale: Secrets must be externalized and never logged or committed

nodes.label: GO-HTTP-001: HTTP servers MUST set timeouts and MaxHeaderBytes
requirements: - MUST set: `ReadHeaderTimeout`, and SHOULD set `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, `IdleTimeout` as appropriate for the service.
- MUST set `MaxHeaderBytes` to a justified limit for your application.
- MUST NOT rely on default zero-values for timeouts in production for internet-facing servers.
fixes: - Use `http.Server{ReadHeaderTimeout: ..., ReadTimeout: ..., WriteTimeout: ..., IdleTimeout: ..., MaxHeaderBytes: ...}`.
- Calibrate timeouts per endpoint type (streaming vs JSON APIs).
nodes.rationale: HTTP servers MUST set timeouts and MaxHeaderBytes

nodes.label: GO-HTTP-002: Request body and multipart parsing MUST be size-bounded
nodes.severity: Medium (DoS risk; can be High for upload-heavy apps)
requirements: - MUST enforce a global maximum request body size for endpoints that accept bodies.
- MUST enforce strict multipart upload limits and avoid unbounded form parsing.
- SHOULD enforce per-route limits when some endpoints legitimately need larger bodies.
- SHOULD set upstream (proxy) limits as defense-in-depth.
fixes: - Wrap request bodies with `http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBytes)` before parsing.
- For multipart, set conservative limits and validate file sizes/part counts explicitly.
- Set proxy limits (e.g., at ingress) in addition to app limits.
nodes.rationale: Request body and multipart parsing MUST be size-bounded

nodes.label: GO-DEPLOY-002: Diagnostic endpoints (pprof/expvar/metrics) MUST NOT be publicly exposed
requirements: - MUST NOT expose `net/http/pprof` handlers on a public internet-facing listener without strong access controls.
- SHOULD run diagnostics on a separate, internal-only listener (loopback/VPC-only) and require auth.
- MUST review what diagnostic endpoints reveal (stack traces, memory, command lines, environment, internal URLs).
fixes: - Remove diagnostics from production builds, or bind them to an internal-only listener.
- Add strong authentication/authorization (and ideally network-level restrictions).
nodes.rationale: Diagnostic endpoints (pprof/expvar/metrics) MUST NOT be publicly exposed

nodes.label: GO-HTTP-003: Reverse proxy and forwarded header trust MUST be explicit
requirements: - If behind a reverse proxy, MUST define which proxy is trusted and how client IP/scheme/host are derived.
- MUST NOT trust `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `Forwarded`, or similar headers from the open internet.
- MUST ensure “secure cookie” logic, redirects, and absolute URL generation do not rely on spoofable headers.
fixes: - Enforce proxy trust at the edge and in app:
- Accept forwarded headers only from known proxy IP ranges.
- Prefer platform-provided mechanisms where available.
- If generating external links, use a configured allowlisted canonical origin (not the request’s Host header).
nodes.rationale: Reverse proxy and forwarded header trust MUST be explicit

nodes.label: GO-HTTP-004: Security headers SHOULD be set (in app or at the edge)
requirements: - SHOULD set:

- `Content-Security-Policy` (CSP) appropriate to the app. NOTE: It is most important to set the CSP's script-src. All other directives are not as important and can generally be excluded for the ease of development.
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- Clickjacking protection (`X-Frame-Options` and/or CSP `frame-ancestors`)
- `Referrer-Policy` and `Permissions-Policy` where appropriate
- MUST ensure cookies have secure attributes (see GO-HTTP-005).
NOTE:
- These headers may be set via reverse proxy/CDN; if not visible in app code, report as “verify at edge”.
fixes: - Add centralized header middleware in Go, or configure at the edge.
- Keep CSP realistic; avoid `unsafe-inline` where possible.
nodes.rationale: Security headers SHOULD be set (in app or at the edge)

nodes.label: GO-HTTP-005: Cookies MUST use secure attributes in production
requirements: - MUST set `Secure` on cookies that carry auth/session state. IMPORTANT NOTE: Only set `Secure` in production environment when TLS is configured. When running in a local dev environment over HTTP, do not set `Secure` property on cookies. You should do this conditionally based on if the app is running in production mode. You should also include a property like `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` which can be used to disable `Secure` cookies when testing over HTTP.
- MUST set `HttpOnly` on auth/session cookies.
- SHOULD set `SameSite=Lax` by default (or `Strict` if compatible), and only use `None` when necessary (and only with `Secure`).
- SHOULD set bounded lifetimes (`Max-Age`/`Expires`) appropriate to the app.
fixes: - Set the correct fields on `http.Cookie` and centralize cookie creation.
nodes.rationale: Cookies MUST use secure attributes in production

nodes.label: GO-HTTP-006: Cookie-authenticated state-changing endpoints MUST be CSRF-protected
requirements: - MUST protect all state-changing endpoints (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) that rely on cookies for authentication.
- SHOULD use a well-tested CSRF library/middleware rather than rolling your own.
- MAY use additional defenses (Origin/Referer checks, Fetch Metadata, SameSite cookies), but tokens remain the primary defense for cookie-authenticated apps.
If tokens are impractical, or for small applications:

* MUST at a minimum require a custom header to be set and set the session cookie SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax, as this is the strongest method besides requiring a form token, and may be much easier to implement.
fixes: - Add CSRF middleware and ensure it covers all state-changing routes.
- If the service is an API intended for non-browser clients, avoid cookie auth; use Authorization headers.
nodes.rationale: Cookie-authenticated state-changing endpoints MUST be CSRF-protected

nodes.label: GO-HTTP-007: CORS must be explicit and least-privilege
requirements: - If CORS is not needed, MUST keep it disabled.
- If CORS is needed:
- MUST allowlist trusted origins (do not reflect arbitrary origins)
- MUST be careful with credentialed requests; do not combine broad origins with cookies
- SHOULD restrict allowed methods/headers
fixes: - Implement strict origin allowlists and minimal methods/headers.
- Ensure cookie-auth endpoints are not exposed cross-origin unless required.
nodes.rationale: CORS must be explicit and least-privilege

nodes.label: GO-XSS-001: Use html/template and avoid bypassing auto-escaping with untrusted data
requirements: - MUST use `html/template` for HTML rendering (not `text/template`).
- MUST NOT convert untrusted data into “trusted” template types (`template.HTML`, `template.JS`, `template.URL`, etc.).
- SHOULD keep templates static and controlled by developers; treat dynamic templates as high risk.
- MUST NOT serve user-uploaded HTML/JS as active content unless explicitly intended and safely sandboxed.
fixes: - Use `html/template` and pass untrusted data as data, not markup.
- If you must allow limited HTML, use a vetted HTML sanitizer and still be careful with attributes/URLs.
nodes.rationale: Use html/template and avoid bypassing auto-escaping with untrusted data

nodes.label: GO-SSTI-001: Never parse/execute templates from untrusted input (SSTI)
requirements: - MUST NOT call `template.Parse` / `template.ParseFiles` / `template.New(...).Parse(...)` on template text influenced by untrusted input.
- MUST treat “user-defined templates” as a special high-risk design:
- MUST use heavy sandboxing and strict allowlists
- MUST isolate execution (process/container boundary) if truly required
fixes: - Replace with safe substitution mechanisms (no code execution).
- If templates must be user-controlled, isolate and sandbox aggressively.
nodes.rationale: Never parse/execute templates from untrusted input (SSTI)

nodes.label: GO-PATH-001: Prevent path traversal and unsafe file serving
requirements: - MUST NOT pass user-controlled paths to `os.Open`, `os.ReadFile`, `http.ServeFile`, or `http.FileServer` without strict validation and base-dir enforcement.
- MUST treat `..`, absolute paths, and OS-specific path tricks as hostile input.
- SHOULD store user uploads outside any static web root; serve through controlled handlers.
- MUST avoid directory listing for sensitive file trees.
fixes: - Use an allowlist of file identifiers (e.g., database IDs) mapped to server-side paths.
- Enforce base directory containment after cleaning and joining.
- Serve active formats as downloads (`Content-Disposition: attachment`) unless explicitly intended.
nodes.rationale: Prevent path traversal and unsafe file serving

nodes.label: GO-UPLOAD-001: File uploads must be validated, stored safely, and served safely
requirements: - MUST enforce upload size limits (app + edge).
- MUST validate file type using allowlists and content checks (not only extensions).
- MUST store uploads outside executable/static roots when possible.
- SHOULD generate server-side filenames (random IDs) and avoid trusting original names.
- MUST serve potentially active formats safely (download attachment) unless explicitly intended.
fixes: - Implement allowlist validation + safe storage + safe serving.
- Add scanning/quarantine workflows where applicable.
nodes.rationale: File uploads must be validated, stored safely, and served safely

nodes.label: GO-INJECT-001: Prevent SQL injection (parameterized queries / ORM)
requirements: - MUST use parameterized queries or an ORM that parameterizes under the hood.
- MUST NOT build SQL by string concatenation / `fmt.Sprintf` / string interpolation with untrusted input.
fixes: - Replace with placeholders (`?`, `$1`, etc.) and pass parameters separately.
- Validate and type-check IDs before use.
nodes.rationale: Prevent SQL injection (parameterized queries / ORM)

nodes.label: GO-INJECT-002: Prevent OS command injection; avoid shelling out with untrusted input
requirements: - MUST avoid executing external commands with attacker-controlled strings.
- If subprocess is necessary:
- MUST use `exec.CommandContext` with an argument list (not `sh -c`).
- MUST NOT pass untrusted input to a shell (`bash -c`, `sh -c`, PowerShell).
- SHOULD use strict allowlists for any variable component (subcommand, flags, filenames).
- MUST assume CLI tools may interpret attacker-controlled args as flags or special values.
fixes: - Use library APIs instead of subprocesses.
- Hardcode command and allowlist/validate args.
- If a shell is unavoidable, escape robustly and treat as high risk (prefer avoiding).
nodes.rationale: Prevent OS command injection; avoid shelling out with untrusted input

nodes.label: GO-SSRF-001: Prevent SSRF in outbound HTTP requests
requirements: - MUST treat outbound requests to user-provided URLs as high risk.
- SHOULD allowlist hosts/domains for any user-influenced URL fetch.
- SHOULD block access to localhost/private IP ranges/link-local addresses and cloud metadata endpoints.
- MUST restrict schemes to `http`/`https` (no `file:`, `gopher:`, etc.).
- MUST set client timeouts and restrict redirects.
fixes: - Parse URLs strictly; enforce scheme and allowlisted hostnames.
- Resolve DNS and enforce IP-range restrictions (with care for DNS rebinding).
- Set timeouts, disable redirects unless needed, and cap response sizes.
nodes.rationale: Prevent SSRF in outbound HTTP requests

nodes.label: GO-HTTPCLIENT-001: Outbound HTTP clients MUST set timeouts and close bodies
requirements: - MUST set an overall timeout on `http.Client` usage (or equivalent per-request deadlines via context + transport timeouts).
- MUST ensure `resp.Body.Close()` is called for all successful requests (typically `defer resp.Body.Close()` immediately after error check).
- SHOULD limit response body reads (do not `io.ReadAll` unbounded responses).
- SHOULD restrict redirects for security-sensitive fetches (SSRF, auth flows).
fixes: - Use a configured client with timeouts.
- Always close response bodies.
- Use bounded readers (`io.LimitReader`) for large/untrusted responses.
nodes.rationale: Outbound HTTP clients MUST set timeouts and close bodies

nodes.label: GO-REDIRECT-001: Prevent open redirects
nodes.severity: Medium (can be High with auth flows)
requirements: - MUST validate redirect targets derived from untrusted input (`next`, `redirect`, `return_to`).
- SHOULD prefer only same-site relative paths.
- SHOULD fall back to a safe default on validation failure.
fixes: - Allowlist internal paths or known domains.
- Reject absolute URLs unless explicitly needed and allowlisted.
nodes.rationale: Prevent open redirects

nodes.label: GO-CRYPTO-001: Cryptographic randomness MUST come from crypto/rand
nodes.severity: High (Critical if used for auth/session tokens or keys)
requirements: - MUST use `crypto/rand` for:
- session IDs, password reset tokens, API keys, CSRF tokens, nonces
- encryption keys, signing keys, salts when required
- MUST NOT use `math/rand` for any security-sensitive value.
- SHOULD use built-in helpers that produce appropriately strong tokens when available.
fixes: - Switch to `crypto/rand` (`rand.Reader`, `rand.Read`, or secure token helpers).
- Ensure sufficient entropy and use URL-safe encoding.
nodes.rationale: Cryptographic randomness MUST come from crypto/rand

nodes.label: GO-AUTH-001: Password storage MUST use adaptive hashing (bcrypt/argon2id) and safe comparisons
requirements: - MUST hash passwords using an adaptive password hashing function (bcrypt or argon2id).
- MUST NOT store plaintext passwords or reversible encryption of passwords.
- MUST compare secrets in constant time when relevant (tokens, MACs, API keys) to reduce timing leaks.
- SHOULD ensure password policies do not exceed algorithm constraints (e.g., bcrypt has input length limits; handle long passphrases appropriately).
fixes: - Use `bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword` / `CompareHashAndPassword` or argon2id with recommended parameters.
- Use constant-time compare helpers when comparing MACs/tokens.
nodes.rationale: Password storage MUST use adaptive hashing (bcrypt/argon2id) and safe comparisons

nodes.label: GO-CONC-001: Data races and concurrency hazards MUST be treated as security-relevant
nodes.severity: Medium to High (depends on what races affect)
requirements: - MUST run tests with the race detector (`go test -race`) in CI for security-sensitive services.
- MUST fix detected races; do not suppress without deep justification.
- SHOULD treat shared mutable state in handlers as high risk; enforce synchronization or avoid shared mutability.
fixes: - Add proper synchronization or redesign to avoid shared mutable state.
- Add race tests and run them continuously.
nodes.rationale: Data races and concurrency hazards MUST be treated as security-relevant

nodes.label: GO-UNSAFE-001: Use of unsafe/cgo MUST be minimized and audited like memory-unsafe code
requirements: - SHOULD avoid importing `unsafe` in application code unless absolutely necessary.
- If `unsafe` is used, MUST treat it as “manual memory safety” requiring careful review and test coverage.
- If `cgo` is used, MUST treat the C/C++ boundary as memory-unsafe; apply secure coding practices on the C side and isolate where possible.
fixes: - Replace unsafe/cgo usage with safe standard library alternatives where possible.
- Isolate unsafe code in small, well-tested modules with fuzz/race tests.
nodes.rationale: Use of unsafe/cgo MUST be minimized and audited like memory-unsafe code

nodes.label: Generation mode in golang-general-backend
nodes.rationale: Apply secure defaults while generating relevant code.

nodes.label: Passive review mode in golang-general-backend
nodes.rationale: Flag major vulnerabilities discovered during relevant editing.

nodes.label: Active audit mode in golang-general-backend
nodes.rationale: Requires an explicit scan request; evidence-based findings guide review.
